subject: Reserved GPU concurrency variance and transient queueing — exception request
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@northstar-payments.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: DevOps Team <ops@northstar-payments.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Production launch traffic spike — reserved GPU concurrency shortfall

Hi Marissa,

Quick heads up from our ops team: during yesterday's feature flag ramp we saw sustained concurrent inference beyond the committed concurrency in our Dedicated pool which led to transient queueing and ~200ms added P95 tail latency for about 18 minutes. The feature launch is next week and we need a temporary headroom carve‑out (additional reserved concurrency) or an SLA exception that prevents queueing for the next 30 days while we complete the rollout.

We'd like to avoid dropping to the fallback model; the quality delta is visible. Can your team provide a short-term reserve (1.3x current) or confirm an exception to the queueing policy?

Attached: traffic_pattern_snapshot.json (stub)

Thanks,
Aisha
Sr. Platform Engineer
NorthStar Payments

---
NorthStar Ops note (excerpt): "window 2026-09-07T18:10Z - 2026-09-07T18:28Z shows sustained 1.4x concurrency vs baseline; KV cache hit ratio unchanged; fallback triggered twice.",
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@northstar-payments.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production launch traffic spike — reserved GPU concurrency shortfall

Aisha — thanks for the signal and for the snapshot. I copied Kar (SRE lead for Dedicated) and Ben (Solutions) so we can move fast.

Short answer: we can do a temporary concurrency carve‑out, but we need to align on:
- exact target concurrency (numbers) and expected steady state vs peak windows
- whether you want a hard reservation (billed as overage or premium reserve) or a policy exception that prioritizes your requests 
- rollback criteria and telemetry we'll monitor (token throughput, queue depth, P95/P99 latency)

Can you share the expected concurrency target for the 30‑day window and confirm you can accept a short term pricing adjustment for reserved headroom? Once we have that, Kar will simulate queueing impact and propose a validated commit number.

Action items:
1) Aisha: provide projected concurrency curve (CSV or brief table) by EOD today.
2) Kar: run simulated reservation impact and confirm whether we need model variant fallback to avoid QoS regressions.
3) Ben: prepare a short addendum (term + pricing) for a temporary reservation.

I'll follow up with a proposed timeline once we have the curve.

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Phone: (415) 555-0126

Attachment references: traffic_pattern_snapshot.json (from NorthStar)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@northstar-payments.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production launch traffic spike — reserved GPU concurrency shortfall

Hi all,

I dug into the snapshot Aisha sent and ran a short simulation against NorthStar's current Dedicated pool. Notes:
- Current reservation: 48 concurrent inference slots across 3 reserved nodes.
- Observed transient peak: ~67 concurrent slots (1.4x).
- Cause: bursty request fan‑out from the gateway during the rollout window; prefix cache warmed but not sufficient for the joint peaks.

Options we can do quickly (24–48 hours):
1) Temporary hard reservation to 64 slots (cost = 0.27x monthly reserved rate pro rata) — guarantees no queueing for requested calls up to that cap.
2) Priority queueing exception: keep reservation at 48 but prioritize NorthStar traffic within the pool during peak windows. This reduces tail latency but still allows limited queueing if absolute concurrency exceeds physical capacity; also requires agreement on acceptance criteria.
3) Hybrid: raise to 56 slots + priority policy to reduce both cost and risk.

Operational considerations:
- If we do (1) we need a signed addendum authorizing the pro‑rata charge and start date.
- If we do (2) we'll instrument a short runbook for on‑call to flip priority policy during the rollout windows and run a 6‑hour smoke validation before your go‑live.
- All options will be accompanied by a temporary SLA exception document enumerating the headroom window, rollback triggers (sustained 5% error or >500ms P95), and telemetry hooks (Latency, Queue Depth, KV hit).

Attachment: capacity_report_202609.pdf (capacity simulation summary)

If NorthStar confirms target and preferred path I can schedule the change and get finance the addendum language.

—Kar
SRE Lead, Dedicated Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@northstar-payments.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 07:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production launch traffic spike — reserved GPU concurrency shortfall

Thanks Kar — that analysis is helpful. NorthStar is comfortable with option (3): raise to 56 slots + priority policy for the next 30 days. We accept a pro‑rata incremental charge and the rollback criteria you listed.

We'll share a 24‑hour traffic curve for the next launch window and we can sign the addendum today if you send it. Please cc our procurement (procurement@northstar-payments.com) on the DocuSign link.

A couple of small asks:
- Can you confirm whether burst queueing events will still count toward our incident metrics for the month (we want to avoid a renewal impact from this temporary window)?
- Can you provide the small set of telemetry dashboards we'll use to validate success?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Aisha

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, procurement@northstar-payments.com

Kar, please provision the reservation and post the telemetry links to the HubSpot record.

I've created a HubSpot task and attached the capacity simulation to the company record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/78910. DocuSign link for signature: https://www.docusign.com/eqr/NSP-commitment-attach

- Aisha: drop the 24‑hour curve into the HubSpot file or reply with the CSV.

Thanks all — we'll treat this as a high‑priority workflow.

—Marissa
